title: Email Marketing for Pet Groomers, Keep Clients Coming Back

facts.fact: Mailchimp is free for up to 500 contacts, according to the page.
facts.quote: Mailchimp (think of it as your email command center) is free for up to 500 contacts, more than enough to get started.

facts.fact: The page lists ActiveCampaign at $15 per month.
The page lists Calendly as free.
The page claims email marketing returns $42 per $1 spent; the page does not name a source for this figure.
The page claims 65% of repeat clients come from referrals; the page does not name a source for this figure.
The page claims email marketing saves about 8 hours per month after setup.
The page states the tutorial takes about 60 minutes to set up.
facts.quote: ⏱ 60 minutes to set up 💰 Free to start 📧 No tech skills needed

facts.fact: The page's template for the welcome sequence's first email is sent immediately after signup.
In the page's welcome sequence, the second email is sent 3 days after the first appointment.
facts.quote: ### Email 2, Sent 3 days after first appointment

facts.fact: In the page's welcome sequence, the third email is sent 5 weeks after the first appointment.
facts.quote: ### Email 3, Sent 5 weeks after first appointment

facts.fact: The page's welcome template promises a reminder 24 hours before each appointment.
facts.quote: We'll send a reminder 24 hours before each visit

facts.fact: The page says Mailchimp requires a physical mailing address for email marketing under CAN-SPAM law, which appears at the bottom of every email.
facts.quote: Mailchimp will ask for a physical mailing address, this is legally required for email marketing (CAN-SPAM law).

facts.fact: The page says Mailchimp adds an unsubscribe link automatically.
facts.quote: always include an unsubscribe link (Mailchimp adds this automatically)
